standard_prerequisites.name: Henselisation of a pair and Gabber's comparison
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Algebra, the description of the henselisation A^h as a filtered colimit of etale A-algebras with A/I = A^h/IA^h, together with the same chapter's henselian-pair comparison theorem
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identification H^q(Z, I|_Z) = H^q(X^h, I|_{X^h}) in the affine case.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of filtered colimits and injectivity on an etale neighbourhood
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the colimit theorem for etale cohomology and the lemma that the restriction of an injective sheaf along an etale morphism is injective
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the colimit presentation of H^q(X^h, I|_{X^h}) and the vanishing of each term of the colimit.

standard_prerequisites.name: Mayer-Vietoris for an open cover with affine intersection
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the Mayer-Vietoris exact sequence for the cover X = U union V used in the induction
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the exact sequence that propagates the vanishing from U, V and U cap V to X.

core_obligations: Affine case n = 0 (proof lines 15269-15291): for X = Spec(A) and Z = Spec(A/I), let A^h be the henselisation, so that (A^h, IA^h) is a henselian pair with A/I = A^h/IA^h; Gabber's theorem identifies H^q(Z, I|_Z) with H^q(X^h, I|_{X^h}), the colimit theorem rewrites the latter as the colimit over the etale A-algebras B defining A^h of H^q(Spec(B), I|_{Spec(B)}), and each of those groups vanishes because the restriction of an injective sheaf along an etale morphism stays injective.

Induction step (proof lines 15293-15306): write X = U union V with U a union of n affine opens and V affine; affineness of the diagonal makes U cap V a union of n affine opens, and Mayer-Vietoris gives the displayed exact sequence relating H^q on Z, on U cap V cap Z and on the pieces; by the induction hypothesis the two outer terms vanish for q > n, hence so does H^q_etale(Z, I|_Z).
This completes the induction on n and gives the bound in the statement (statement lines 15258-15266).
proof_roadmap: Handle the affine case by replacing A with its henselisation along I, applying Gabber's comparison, and evaluating the resulting colimit with injectivity on etale neighbourhoods.
Induct on n using the cover X = U union V, affineness of the diagonal to control U cap V, and the Mayer-Vietoris exact sequence.
difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the cohomological dimension of a closed subscheme with affine-module coefficients: for X with affine diagonal covered by n+1 affine opens, H^q_etale(Z, I|_Z) = 0 for q > n (statement lines 15258-15266). The proof (proof lines 15268-15306) proves the affine case by passing to the henselisation of the pair, invoking the henselian-pair comparison, and evaluating the resulting filtered colimit through injectivity of the restriction along etale morphisms; the general case follows by induction using Mayer-Vietoris for a cover by a union of n affine opens and one affine open, with affineness of the diagonal controlling the intersection. H2: one affine computation plus an induction on the number of affine opens.
